name: The Graham household — a name from the post office's letter lists
head: graham_john

arrival.note: A BOUND FROM THE RETURN, NOT AN ARRIVAL. The office's list of letters uncalled-for is a RETURN — its statement of what was still unclaimed on ONE day — and the paper reprinted one return over as many consecutive issues as it took, so the bound is dated by the return of 1 July 1834 and not by the issue it was read in (T-0425). The earliest issue this project reads the name in is 1834-07-09, 8 days later; that gap is an accident of which impression an extraction pass reached, and it is not evidence. Somebody was writing to this name at Chicago by 1834-07-01 and at no stated time before it; nothing says when they came. The date lines the printings set, and how they were weighed, stand beside this rule in tools/mint_letter_list_residents.py.

arrival_year.note: DRAWN, NOT READ. The household's arrival block holds a BOUND — somebody was here by 1834-07-01 and no source says when they came — so the year is drawn from the arrival years the known layer records, truncated at that bound and renormalised. It says what a household of this bound most likely was, and nothing whatever about this household.

It is the only origin distribution this project holds and this value is drawn from it, not measured.

last_dated_appearance.note: A DATED READING OF THIS PERSON, AND THE LAST ONE THE CORPUS HOLDS. Read from `letter_list_returns` as `1834-07-09`, which reaches 1834-07-09 — 357 day(s) short of 1835-07-01. A RETURN IS A DATE AND NOT A CITATION: `letter_list_returns` carries no source per return, so this leg cites none and the corpus that printed it is named in the person's own `sources`. THE FIELD IS THE EVIDENCE UNDER THE VERDICT, not a new claim: nothing here moves the presence off `uncertain`, and T-1159 and T-1172 classify this household by this date instead of reading it out of the prose (T-1144 acceptance 9).

present_on_scene_date.note: THE CORPUS STOPS BEFORE THE SCENE DATE. Nothing after 1834-07-16 follows this person to 1 July 1835 or says they left. `uncertain` rather than dropped — the distinction index.json draws for Jeremiah Porter, and a finding, not a gap.

persons.note: PROJECTED RESIDENT. Documented in Chicago post-office evidence but not independently corroborated strongly enough for attested circa-1835 residence. KNOWN ONLY FROM THE POST OFFICE, IN ONE RETURN. The papers print 'John Graham' and 'lohn Graham' in a single return of letters uncalled-for at the Chicago post office — the Democrat of 9 July 1834, column 9, reprinted over 2 consecutive issues — dated 1834-07-09 to 1834-07-16. Nothing else in the corpus names this person: no trade, no street, no household, no arrival, so every other claim here is written unattested in its own block. WHAT THAT IS WORTH: a correspondent believed a person of this name reachable at Chicago on that date, and nothing further — not that they lived here, kept a trade here, or were here on 1 July 1835. It is the weakest evidence this project accepts for a resident, and a source placing them elsewhere retires the record. THE ARGUMENT EVERY RECORD OF THIS KIND SHARES is written once instead of once per file: the ruling of 2026-08-30 and what it cost the town (docs/LIBERTIES.md L214), the refusals and the transcription standard behind the reading (tools/mint_letter_list_residents.py). No figure is drawn (L1).

age_band.note: THE BAND THIS PERSON'S OWN BIRTH YEAR PUTS THEM IN on 1 July 1835. It is a view of a value already on this card and adds nothing to it; it exists so the age axis can be read across the whole layer at once, beside the bands the model draws for everybody else.

sex_basis.note: A FORENAME THAT STANDS IN ONE SEX'S NAMING ONLY. 'John' is read as male because 14 persons in this layer whose sex a source records bear it (bates_john_jr, calhoun_john, caton_john_dean, davis_john, greene_john, hogan_john_s_c, and others), and it stands in the irish and yankee male forename pool of this town's own attested naming. Nothing about this person is recorded; the name is the whole of the reasoning, and the table that licenses it — data/research/residents/forename_sex.json — refuses a name its own evidence splits, refuses Jean, Marion, Leslie and Francis by name, and refuses an initial outright.

birth_year.note: A BIRTH INTERVAL OUT OF A DEATH NOTICE, NOT A RECORD OF A BIRTH. The page prints the death as 'December 28, 1865' and the age as 'aged 73'. An age of 73 completed years means at least 73 and less than 74, so the birth falls between 1791-12-29 and 1792-12-28: the birth year is 1791 or 1792. The subtraction is this project's; the page states no year of birth. Fergus's 1843 directory (1896) prints the entry "Graham, Gen. James Duncan, died December 28, 1865, aged 73.", and its header admits the list also names citizens who arrived after 1843 and others merely prominently connected with Illinois history — so a match here is never evidence of residence in 1835 and never moves a grade. The match to this person was adjudicated in data/research/old_settlers/death_notices_crosswalk_1835.json and written onto this card by tools/spend_old_settlers.py; this pass only spends its arithmetic into a birth year. Both sides of the match spell a forename out — the crosswalk's thin matches, where a single initial is the whole of the discriminator, are refused rather than spent.

research_note: MINTED FROM THE LETTER LISTS (T-0378, T-0379). THE HOUSEHOLD IS A CONTAINER, NOT AN ARGUMENT: every other record here argues for a household, and this one argues for a PERSON. `data/residents/` cannot carry a person outside a household, so one was written around them and told to claim nothing — one member, no dwelling, no division, no trade, no family, no arrival beyond the paper's bound. tools/mint_letter_list_residents.py derives the set and prints every refusal, `--gate` proves no record here gained a roof, a trade or a second member, and docs/LIBERTIES.md L214 carries the change of scale.

old_settler_deaths.the_header_admission:
Names, places * , dates, and ages at death
of some of Chicago's Old Settlers, prior to 1843, and other well - known citizens who arrived after 1843, together
with others prominently connected with Illinois history:
old_settler_deaths.note: LATER EVIDENCE OF A DEATH, BESIDE THE 1835 CLAIMS AND NOT INSIDE THEM. Fergus's 1843 directory (1896) prints an obituary list of old settlers, and one of its entries meets somebody of this name. THE HEADER OF THE LIST IS QUOTED ABOVE, and it is the limit the whole reading turns on. It does not mean the person was in Chicago in 1835, and it does not mean they arrived before 1843 — the list's own header, quoted above, says it also names citizens who arrived later and others merely 'prominently connected with Illinois history'. A match means one thing: a name in the 1835 layer and a name in this list agree on surname and first initial, and the list gives that name a death date and an age. The date and the interval are the payload. Whatever is carried is carried as evidence of a DEATH and of an interval the birth falls in, never as an 1835 fact and never as a grade. T-0513 consolidates and T-0514/T-0515 apply; this file changes no record. This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE. A death notice printed in 1896 says a person of this name died on a day; under the ratified ladder (T-0513) that is later evidence about a DEATH, and it is never an 1835 residence. T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once; this pass hands it the evidence and not the verdict.
